title: Quentin and the Orbit
premise: Zephyrine Sterling, a xenolinguist stationed on the dying colony of Meridian's Rest, has begun dreaming in a language no human speaks — the tongue of the orbiting alien structure locals call the Orbit. When the colony's children begin sharing his dream, he discovers the Orbit is not dying but grieving, and that two rival fleets circling above are one misstep from war over it. To save both the colony and the children, Zephyrine sustains a fabricated translation — a lie of peace — that keeps the fleets talking instead of firing. As the truce expires, he must choose between confessing the lie and losing the belonging he finally found, and in doing so he learns the dream-language was never the aliens' at all: it was Meridian's Rest itself, remembered by the Orbit after the colonists' original ship was lost. The novel ends with Zephyrine speaking truth to both fleets, the truce holding on fragile honesty, and him staying behind as the colony's living archive.
about_author: Coral Hartwell is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent six years documenting endangered languages before turning to fiction. They write quiet, aching science fiction about people who translate themselves into strangers.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. On forgotten Meridian's Rest, Zephyrine records the colony's final dialects while hiding that he now dreams in an alien language. A supply ship skips the colony without landing. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into dread — he realizes no one is coming, and something in the sky is listening to him.

chapters.title: Children of the Shared Dream
chapters.summary: POV alternating Zephyrine and nine-year-old Ilsa Vann. The colony's children wake reciting identical phrases — Zephyrine's dream-tongue, word for word. Parents panic; the council blames contamination. Emotional beat: uncanny tenderness; Zephyrine recognizes himself in the children and feels, for the first time, less alone.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Sky
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. He decodes the children's dream: the Orbit is broadcasting grief, and two rival fleets — Commonwealth and Concord — have arrived claiming salvage rights over it. The colony becomes a bargaining chip neither side will admit to holding. Emotional beat: vertigo; the forgotten place is suddenly the most important in the system.

chapters.title: The Truce Table
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine as reluctant translator. Summoned to the flagship, he invents a 'diplomatic register' of the alien language that doesn't exist, buying a thirty-day truce by making each fleet believe the other wants peace. Emotional beat: guilty exhilaration — the lie works, and he hates how good he is at it.

chapters.title: What the Orbit Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa, with Zephyrine. In a shared dream, the children show Zephyrine the Orbit's memory: the colonists' original generation ship, lost centuries ago, absorbed and mourned. The Orbit isn't invading — it's keeping the dead colony's voice alive. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak; belonging means inheriting grief.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The lie compounds: each fleet demands proof of the other's goodwill, and Zephyrine fabricates transmissions nightly while the colony starves quietly below. His old mentor, Commander Reyes, grows suspicious of his translations. Emotional beat: suffocation; duty and love pull in opposite directions as he falls for fleet medic Anouk, who sees through him.

chapters.title: The Confession He Can't Make
chapters.summary: POV Anouk. Anouk discovers the fabricated transmissions but says nothing, torn between her oath and her love for Zephyrine. Meanwhile the children's dreams intensify — they've begun sleepwalking toward the upland beacon. Emotional beat: aching intimacy; she chooses to protect his secret, knowing it may doom them all.

chapters.title: Expiry
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The truce expires mid-negotiation when Reyes exposes the fake register. Both fleets arm; the Orbit responds by amplifying the children's dream across every mind in orbit, including the fleets'. Panic spreads ship to ship. Emotional beat: collapse — the lie dies, and only the truth remains, screaming in everyone's head at once.

chapters.title: Speaking the Dead Language
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, climax. Standing between the fleets on open channels, Zephyrine abandons translation and speaks the Orbit's true message: the names of the lost generation ship's crew, sung back by the children below. Grief does what diplomacy couldn't. Emotional beat: catharsis; enemies weep at the same funeral, and the ceasefire holds because it is honest.

chapters.title: Meridian's Rest
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, epilogue. The fleets withdraw, leaving a joint stewardship; aid finally lands. Offered rescue and a chair at the Commonwealth academy, Zephyrine chooses to stay as the colony's archivist, with Anouk beside him and the children dreaming freely. Emotional beat: quiet arrival home — identity, love, and belonging resolved into one chosen life.
